entries.title: Isaiah 38:12
segments: From day even to night; day and night, that is by a sickness that has no intermission.  Compare

. 
 
No age, nor strength, nor station can exempt us from liability to sudden death in the midst of our cherished enterprises.  It is our wisdom to hold ourselves always ready to leave this life with all its labors, at God's bidding.

entries.title: Isaiah 38:13
segments: The best relief in times of deep anguish, is to pour out our hearts to God in prayer.

entries.title: Isaiah 38:15
segments:
What shall I say? this verse refers to God's second message promising him restoration from his present sickness. 
 
  In the bitterness of my soul; in humility and contrition, from the remembrance of this chastisement.

The remembrance of past afflictions should fill us with humility in view of the sinfulness which made them necessary, and with gratitude in view of God's undeserved goodness in delivering us from them.

entries.title: Isaiah 38:16
segments: By these things--in all these things; by God's forgiving love and healing power.

entries.title: Isaiah 38:17
segments: Cast all my sins behind thy back; forgiven them.  Hezekiah regards his sickness as a chastisement for his sins.  Compare

segments: Cannot praise thee; see note on

. 
 
  Hope for thy truth; for the further manifestation of it in this world. 
 
Good men desire the continuance of life mainly for the opportunities which it gives of glorifying God before their fellow men.
